# Region { #timetoalign.timelines.Region }

```python
timelines.Region(
    start,
    end,
    name=None,
    meta=dict(),
    *,
    id=None,
    _minted=False,
    _unknown_keys=dict[str, Any](),
    _statement_state=dict(),
    _prefixes=dict(),
)
```

An identified part of a timeline defined by a TimeInterval.

IMPORTANT: Regions are NOT timelines. They cannot hold events or C-maps.
Use ``Timeline.create_child_from_region(region_id)`` to create a Child
timeline from a Region.

A region is frozen: :meth:`with_statement` and its siblings return a
copy holding other statements (see
:mod:`~timetoalign.timelines.statements`), and a timeline stores a
changed copy in the region's place with
:meth:`Timeline.replace_region <timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.replace_region>`.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                                               |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| start  | [Coordinate](`timetoalign.core.Coordinate`)         | Start coordinate of the region.                           |
| end    | [Coordinate](`timetoalign.core.Coordinate`)         | End coordinate of the region.                             |
| name   | [str](`str`) \| None                                | Optional display name (e.g., "Chorus"); names may repeat. |
| meta   | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | Additional metadata (e.g., traversal order labels).       |
| id     | [str](`str`)                                        | The region's id; minted as ``region_{N}`` when not given. |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign import Coordinate, TimeUnit
>>> start = Coordinate(16.0, TimeUnit.quarters)
>>> end = Coordinate(32.0, TimeUnit.quarters)
>>> region = Region(start, end, name="Chorus")
>>> region.id
'region_1'
>>> region.duration
Duration(Fraction(16, 1), quarters)
>>> region.as_interval
Interval(start=Coordinate(Fraction(16, 1), quarters), end=Coordinate(Fraction(32, 1), quarters))
```

A region marks part of a timeline; turning it into a Child timeline
goes through the timeline that owns it:

```python
>>> from timetoalign import ContinuousLogicalTimeline
>>> tl = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=64)
>>> tl.create_region(16, 32, id="chorus", name="Chorus")
Region('chorus', name='Chorus', 16-32 quarters)
>>> chorus_child = tl.create_child_from_region("chorus")
>>> chorus_child.length
Coordinate(Fraction(16, 1), quarters)
```

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [contains](#timetoalign.timelines.Region.contains) | Check if a coordinate is within this region (left-inclusive). |

| [overlaps](#timetoalign.timelines.Region.overlaps) | Check if this region overlaps with another. |

| [with_prefix](#timetoalign.timelines.Region.with_prefix) | Return a copy declaring a prefix its statements may use. |
| [with_statement](#timetoalign.timelines.Region.with_statement) | Return a copy stating the pair ``(property, value)``; this region is left as it is. |
| [with_verb](#timetoalign.timelines.Region.with_verb) | Return a copy stating a verb of the catalogue in one system's vocabulary. |

### contains { #timetoalign.timelines.Region.contains }

```python
timelines.Region.contains(coord)
```

Check if a coordinate is within this region (left-inclusive).

Following TTA convention, intervals are [start, end) - left-inclusive,
right-exclusive.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                                                                                                                                   | Description                    | Default    |
|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|------------|
| coord  | [int](`int`) \| [float](`float`) \| [Fraction](`fractions.Fraction`) \| [Coordinate](`timetoalign.core.Coordinate`) \| [IdCoordinate](`timetoalign.core.IdCoordinate`) | The coordinate value to check. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type           | Description                   |
|--------|----------------|-------------------------------|
|        | [bool](`bool`) | True if start <= coord < end. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                              |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If a coordinate object's unit differs from the region's. |

### from_dict { #timetoalign.timelines.Region.from_dict }

```python
timelines.Region.from_dict(data, *, unit, number_type)
```

Restore a region from its object in a timeline's ``regions``.

``start`` and ``end`` are bare values on the timeline's axis, which
*unit* and *number_type* describe; ``name``, ``meta``,
``statements`` and ``provenance`` may be left out. Keys the library
does not know are kept and written back. The prefixes the statements
need are the manifest's, which its reader sets.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                | Description                                  | Default    |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|------------|
| data        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | The region object.                           | _required_ |
| unit        | [TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.TimeUnit`)             | The unit of the timeline holding the region. | _required_ |
| number_type | [NumberType](`timetoalign.core.NumberType`)         | The number type of that timeline.            | _required_ |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                           |
|--------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the object is malformed or a value is represented otherwise than the axis selects. |

### overlaps { #timetoalign.timelines.Region.overlaps }

```python
timelines.Region.overlaps(other)
```

Check if this region overlaps with another.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                             | Description                      | Default    |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|------------|
| other  | [Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`) | Another Region to check against. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type           | Description                                          |
|--------|----------------|------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [bool](`bool`) | True if the regions overlap (share any coordinates). |

### with_belief { #timetoalign.timelines.Region.with_belief }

```python
timelines.Region.with_belief(
    property,
    value,
    *,
    actor,
    belief,
    date=None,
    note=None,
    node=(),
)
```

Return a copy recording *actor*'s belief in the pair ``(property, value)``.

See :meth:`MutableStatementsMixin.add_belief
<timetoalign.timelines.MutableStatementsMixin.add_belief>`.

### with_candidate { #timetoalign.timelines.Region.with_candidate }

```python
timelines.Region.with_candidate(
    property,
    value,
    *,
    stated_by,
    method,
    date=None,
    service=None,
    basis=(),
    match=None,
    note=None,
```

See :meth:`MutableStatementsMixin.add_candidate

### with_prefix { #timetoalign.timelines.Region.with_prefix }

```python
timelines.Region.with_prefix(name, namespace)
```

Return a copy declaring a prefix its statements may use.

See :meth:`MutableStatementsMixin.add_prefix
<timetoalign.timelines.MutableStatementsMixin.add_prefix>`.

### with_statement { #timetoalign.timelines.Region.with_statement }

```python
timelines.Region.with_statement(
    property,
    value,
    *,
    node=(),
    provenance=None,
    actor=None,
    date=None,
)
```

Return a copy stating the pair ``(property, value)``; this region is left as it is.

See :meth:`MutableStatementsMixin.add_statement
<timetoalign.timelines.MutableStatementsMixin.add_statement>`.

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign import Coordinate, TimeUnit
>>> intro = Region(Coordinate(0, TimeUnit.quarters), Coordinate(12, TimeUnit.quarters))
>>> described = intro.with_statement("rdfs:comment", "the opening")
>>> intro.statements, described.statements
({}, {'rdfs:comment': ['the opening']})
```

### without_statement { #timetoalign.timelines.Region.without_statement }

